Summary: God's covenant command to Abraham: every man child among you shall be circumcised on the eighth day, as the token of the covenant between God and Abraham's seed (Genesis 17:10-12). The sign was cut into the flesh of the household — sons, servants, and all — marking them as covenant people.
Commandment: Circumcise every male child, as the sign of God's covenant with Abraham.
Application: The sign marked Abraham's household as God's own, and the uncircumcised male was cut off from his people (Genesis 17:14). Debated: Jews continue circumcision as the covenant sign; the New Testament holds it is not required for Gentile believers (Galatians 5:2-6; Acts 15), with circumcision of the heart as the fulfilment. This row does not settle that difference.
Purpose: To mark Abraham's seed with the sign of the everlasting covenant in their flesh (Genesis 17:11-13); the sign's ongoing force is the debated point, not its original purpose.
